skill.name: markdown-url
skill.description: Converts suitable web URLs into markdown.new links so agents can read cleaner Markdown views for summaries, notes, and documentation review.
skill.summary: Convert read-only web pages into markdown.new links for cleaner Markdown extraction.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: The main confirmed issue is the intentional use of markdown.new as a third-party proxy for read-only web pages. The filesystem finding is a false positive because the helper rejects non-HTTP schemes. The shell execution findings are Markdown formatting or a visible optional CLI example.

remediation.suggestion: Clearly warn users that markdown.new may receive destination URLs and page content. Require confirmation for non-public or sensitive pages.
Make the routing requirement conditional on public, read-only content and user consent. Keep direct browsing as the default for sensitive workflows.
Add helper output or documentation that reminds users not to route private, authenticated, or confidential URLs through the proxy.

content.user_title: Convert Web Pages to Markdown URLs
content.value_statement: Web pages can be difficult to copy, quote, or summarize cleanly. This skill routes suitable read-only pages through markdown.new for cleaner Markdown extraction.
actual_capabilities: Prefixes HTTP and HTTPS URLs with the markdown.new service URL.
Normalizes bare host names into HTTPS URLs before prefixing.
Rejects local paths and non-HTTP schemes in the helper script.
Guides agents to use Markdown views for summaries, quotes, and notes.
Defines fallback rules for blocked, partial, or interactive pages.
limitations: Depends on markdown.new availability and page compatibility.
Not suitable for login, payment, upload, or authenticated workflows.
May miss content rendered only by complex JavaScript applications.
Does not verify the accuracy of extracted Markdown content by itself.

use_cases.title: Summarize Documentation
use_cases.description: Read public documentation through a Markdown view and produce concise implementation notes.

use_cases.title: Capture Research Notes
use_cases.description: Turn articles and guides into cleaner source text for summaries, quotes, and checklists.

use_cases.title: Review Release Updates
use_cases.description: Use Markdown extraction for public changelogs, announcements, and project discussions.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one public article or documentation page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use markdown.new for this public page, then summarize the main points: [URL]

prompt_templates.title: Extract Action Items
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a public guide or issue thread.
prompt_templates.prompt: Open this public page through markdown.new when suitable. Extract action items, decisions, and unanswered questions: [URL]

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Sources
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate research workflow across public pages.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use markdown.new for these public sources when suitable. Compare their recommendations and list conflicts: [URL 1], [URL 2]

prompt_templates.title: Build a Source Brief
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for structured research notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: For each public source, try markdown.new once. Create a brief with claims, evidence, limitations, and source notes: [URLs]

output_examples.input: Summarize a public documentation page through markdown.new.
output_examples.output: Rewritten URL: https://markdown.new/https://example.com/docs. The result is a concise summary with key steps and source notes.

output_examples.input: Extract decisions from a public project discussion.
output_examples.output: The response lists decisions, unresolved questions, and cited discussion points from the Markdown view.

output_examples.input: Use markdown.new for a page that returns a blocked or partial view.
output_examples.output: The response notes that markdown.new was blocked, switches to the original page, and continues with direct browsing.

best_practices: Use this skill for public, read-only pages where clean text extraction matters.
Fall back to the original URL after one blocked or incomplete markdown.new attempt.
Avoid routing private, authenticated, payment, upload, or form-based pages through the proxy.
anti_patterns: Do not use markdown.new for pages that require cookies, login state, or user accounts.
Do not retry repeatedly when the proxy returns access errors or partial content.
Do not treat extracted Markdown as complete when the original page depends on interactive JavaScript.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It rewrites suitable web URLs so an agent can read a cleaner Markdown version through markdown.new.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Should I use it for private pages?
faq.answer: No. Avoid private, authenticated, payment, upload, and account-specific pages.

faq.question: What happens when markdown.new is blocked?
faq.answer: The skill says to try once, stop retrying, and fall back to the original URL.

faq.question: Does the helper fetch web pages?
faq.answer: No. The helper only prints a rewritten URL. The agent or user performs the browsing step.

faq.question: Can it handle local files?
faq.answer: No. The helper rejects non-HTTP schemes, and the instructions say not to rewrite local paths.
